lessons: CRITICAL FIX: an incorporated claimant cannot use Small Claims at all. Kolzchut is explicit: 'חברה בע"מ, שותפות או עמותה לא יוכלו להגיש תביעה לבית משפט זה'. The skill said 'Individuals and businesses (osek murshe/patur)' and never stated the bar, so an incorporated freelancer would have been routed to a forum that would strike or transfer the claim. Added as the FIRST gating question in both languages and in the reference.

CRITICAL FIX: 'Magistrate Court requires legal representation' was asserted four times and is false. There is no representation requirement in Israeli civil courts; it is advisable, not mandatory. Overstating it pushes users with claims just over the ceiling to abandon collection.

CORRECTED the section-4 interest mechanism. The law adds 'בתוספת ריבית שקלית, ובחלוף 30 ימים מהמועד האמור - בתוספת דמי פיגורים': ribit shkalit from the payment due date, dmei pigurim only 30 days later. The skill said dmei pigurim run from the due date at 'the Accountant General's rate', which is wrong on both the component and the timing, and the Accountant General framing is obsolete since the rates are now set and published quarterly under Amendment 9.

CORRECTED a Hebrew-only overstatement that a person may file at most 5 small claims per calendar year. The real rule is a declaration duty (תקנה 3(ג)(7): 'מספר התביעות הקטנות שהגיש במהלך השנה האחרונה') plus a discretionary power under sec. 60 of the Courts Law to TRANSFER a case to Magistrate Court when more than five were filed that year. The sixth claim is not barred.

REMOVED an unsourced statutory claim: 'A 2024 amendment gives small contractors on sub-75,000 NIS public-sector contracts a 30-day term.' Nevo's text of the law contains no 75,000 threshold and no small-contractor 30-day term. Removed rather than shipped, per the anti-fabrication rule.

REMOVED a fabricated evidentiary claim that 'English-only reminders lack legal standing in Israeli small claims court.' No such rule. Foreign-language documents are admissible and the court may require a certified translation, so the practical advice (write in Hebrew to Hebrew-speaking clients) was kept and the invented legal proposition dropped.
SOFTENED an overstatement that registered mail is presumed received under Israeli law. It is strong evidence of dispatch; whether receipt is legally deemed depends on the applicable service rules.

RENAMED the generated document. It was called מכתב התחייבות (a letter of UNDERTAKING, which is what a debtor gives) throughout the instruction layer, while the templates correctly produced a demand letter. Now מכתב דרישה / מכתב התראה לפני נקיטת הליכים.

ADDED a deliberately unquantified pointer to VAT bad-debt relief (חוב אבוד). An osek murshe has already remitted the VAT on an unpaid invoice, and the collection trail this skill builds is the evidence that route requires. The eligibility windows are NOT stated because they were not sourced this cycle; the user is told to confirm them with their accountant or the VAT Authority.

PROCESS: the first pass of this cycle fixed the 5-claims rule in SKILL_HE.md and left the contradictory English bullet standing two lines below its own replacement. Both reviewers caught it. This is the third consecutive skill in this batch where a correction was applied to one file and not propagated. Grep the old value across the whole folder before running the panel, every time.

VERIFIED AND KEPT (do not re-litigate): the skill's statement that Israeli law applies simple interest and that Amendment 9 eliminated compounding is CORRECT. Nevo shows section 7 (ריבית דריבית) marked (בוטל) and 'דמי פיגורים לא יצורפו לקרן העדכנית'. A research subagent claimed the opposite (annual compounding); direct verification refuted it.

CARRY: the limitation citation is wrong in four places. The 7-year period for an ordinary debt is sec. 5(1) of חוק ההתיישנות ('בשאינו מקרקעין - שבע שנים'), not sec. 5(a), and the 25-year judgment period is sec. 21. The evidence entry for it also cites a 404 Nevo URL with a paraphrased snippet.

CARRY: references/legal-escalation.md still says the statutory rate is 'Bank of Israel base rate + statutory margin', which is both wrong post-Amendment 9 and contradicts the skill's own four-times-repeated ban on quoting the BoI rate. The Reference Links row for boi.org.il is labelled as the source of statutory interest and should be relabelled or removed.

CARRY: refusing to state an interest rate is the right call, but it is not actionable. The only rate URL in the skill is the BoI page it forbids using. Add the actual publisher of the quarterly ribit shkalit / ribit tzmuda / dmei pigurim rates, and give the agent the always-safe fallback of demanding 'הקרן בתוספת ריבית והצמדה כדין ממועד הפירעון' with no figure.

CARRY: the aging buckets are anchored to days since invoice ISSUE while Step 1 correctly computes lateness from the DUE date. For a private-business client on the statutory shotef+45 default, the day-30 and often day-45 reminders fire before the money is due.

CARRY: the Stage 5 demand-letter template satisfies only about two of the six mandatory contents the skill's own Step 4 lists. It lacks creditor and debtor identification with ח.פ./ע.מ. numbers and addresses, invoice itemisation, enclosures, signature block and a reservation of rights.

CARRY: the escalation ladder omits its cheapest rung, converting the debt into a directly enforceable instrument (post-dated cheques or a שטר חוב) while leverage still exists, so enforcement can skip court. Also missing: pre-escalation entity verification at רשם החברות, retention lien (עיכבון), and giving a settlement the force of a judgment.
CARRY: enforcement is described only as liens and garnishment. The tools that actually make a solvent debtor pay (הגבלות on licence, passport, cheques and credit cards, plus חקירת יכולת) are absent.
